items.name: Power-width interchange and its recurrence (Proposition prop:power-interchange; eq:swap-recurrence)
items.statement: For chunks of $e=m^k$ radix-$q$ digits with a row field divisible by $W^k$: split rows cyclically into $W$ role streams, run the bit network with shear frames (each edge by recursive interchanges, matrix-shear), get $H\gets H+D$ on every row, and interchange by $D\gets D-H,\ H\gets H+D,\ D\gets H-D$. With $s$ calls on volume $V/W$ and a fixed-tape depth-first schedule costing $O(V)$ per node, $F_0=O(1)$, $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$, so $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.
items.role: The recursive saving for address movement: the O(V e^tau) bound that arbitrary-width-interchange extends to all widths.

items.name: Precision and exact recovery (subsection 'Precision and exact recovery'; eq:source-error, eq:final-error)
items.statement: Error bounds chain through contractions with disk margins: ring convolution $E_{\rm ring}<5TL$, chirp $<8TL$, source transform $E_s=9\cdot2^\gamma TL$, then $E_w=S(3E_s+2)<28\cdot2^\gamma T^2L$; after the scales the coefficient error is $<448b\,2^{-b+\gamma}\le448b\,2^{-3b/4}<\tfrac12$ (using $\gamma\le b/4$), so rounding gives the exact integers $0\le c_j<2^{3b}$, and radix-$2^b$ carry propagation gives the $2n$-bit product.
items.role: Proves the output is exactly correct, which the main theorem asserts for every input; this is where p=6b and gamma=o(b) are needed.

items.name: The complete time bound (subsection 'The complete time bound'; Table tab:costs, eq:margin-list)
items.statement: With $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$, every cost divided by $V$ is a power of $p$: $dK$, $pK^{\tau-1}$, $\ell d^{\lambda'}$, $d^2(1+\ell^\tau)$, $dp^{1/2+\delta}\alpha$, $dp^\delta$, $\log(rp)$; their margins below one are $g_1..g_7$ with $\min_ig_i=g_2=\epsilon c(1-\tau)=2^{-181}=2\kappa$. Setup and exceptional-address sorting are $o(V)$, any fixed power of $\log p$ is $\le p^\kappa$, so the time is $O(Tp\,p^{1-\kappa})=O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, with schoolbook multiplication below a cutoff.
items.role: The final step to Theorem thm:main.

items.name: Why the bound disproves the n log n conjecture in this model ('Lower-bound scope and matrix transposition')
items.statement: An eventual lower bound would require $T_A(n)\ge c_An\lg n$ for all large $n$ for every machine; one machine with $\liminf T_A(n)/(n\lg n)=0$ refutes it, and $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ gives limit zero along all lengths.
items.role: Turns the time bound into the 'disproving' clause of the wiki's target.
